relevance_note: Review whose Table 1 lists 24 previously published individuals (columns A1-K1) with individual LPIN2 mutations and clinical features: "only 24 individuals from 10 families with molecularly confirmed Majeed syndrome have been reported in the literature (Table 1)".
method_note: Review; all 24 people come from Table 1, where patients are columns labelled A1..K1 under the column header row (labels used verbatim, rule 1). A Python script in my scratch directory transcribed Table 1 cell by cell (spans = row from its row label through that patient's cell); I checked the parsed cells against the table. Family label = the letter of the column label, supported by the legend ('family A', '(A) Majeed 1989' etc.); source_reference_in_review = the legend's per-family citation. The legend defines '− = not present' with a minus sign (U+2212) while the table cells use an en dash (U+2013); I treated the en-dash cells as that defined symbol and recorded them as excluded with the legend quoted. NR, ND, '?' and empty cells were recorded as not reported. Bare numbers in the Microcytic anemia row (H1 '9.3 MCV', I1 '6.9', J1 '8.5', K1 '10.1') are not defined in the legend and were not recorded; '+°' (anemic, MCV not reported) and '+*' (mild anemia, MCV 86.8) were recorded as anemia, not microcytic anemia, so the checklist item is not reported for D1, D2, E2. Neutropenia row label is split across lines; spans use the '**(ANC)**' line plus '| **Neutropenia**'. E1 'leuko' recorded as observed 'leuko' (undefined abbreviation), checklist neutropenia not reported. '–' in Objective joint swelling does not exclude the composite checklist item 'joint or limb swelling'; '–' in Hepatosplenomegaly is not used to exclude hepatomegaly or splenomegaly separately. CNO '+' mapped to the checklist item chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis (the paper uses CNO as an alternative name for CRMO); F2 bone biopsy 'necrosis' mapped to osteonecrosis using the text 'the seventh demonstrating osteonecrosis'. Zygosity: homozygous for 22 people from 'All patients reported to date have been homozygous with only two patients having a compound heterozygous genotype [81,82]' (refs 81 Bhuyan = K, 82 Liu = J), plus Roy et al.'s family of 6 for I1-I6; K1 compound heterozygous from '(Table 1, K1)' sentence; J1 from refs [81,82] mapped through the legend '(J) Liu'. Variant strings are the protein-level strings from the Mutation row (no 'p.' prefix printed in the table); J1 and K1 cells hold two variants each, split into two rows sharing the cell span. Contradictions: the table lists family I's mutation as 'R736H' while the text says 'proline at amino acid 736 to a histidine (p.P736H)' for Roy et al.; variant type/pathogenicity for family I left not reported because of this mismatch. The text says '24 individuals from 10 families' but the table has 11 family letters; the text notes Al-Mosawi 2007 and 2019 (C and H) are the same extended family. Text also says 'Two brothers from the initial family' had neutrophilic dermatosis and that Majeed 1989 family was consanguineous, but the table legend gives Majeed 1989 for both A and B, so sex and consanguinity were not assigned to individual columns. Out of scope (no individual-level detail or no LPIN2 variant/diagnosis): five Turkish FMF patients heterozygous for LPIN2 variants (counts only), and the Milledge FMF/CDA child (no LPIN2 testing; authors only 'posit' Majeed syndrome).
